chunks: With this chain of transmission, from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from 'Abd Allah ibn Sinan, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

The one who washes the dead body must perform ghusl. If a person kisses the dead after his death while he is still warm, then no ghusl is upon him; but if he touches him and kisses him after he has become cold, then ghusl is obligatory upon him. There is no harm in touching him after the ghusl and kissing him.

key_terms.بَرَدَ: became cold, indicating the condition after which ghusl applies
key_terms.غَسَّلَ: washed, referring to washing the deceased
key_terms.غُسْلٌ: ritual bath that becomes obligatory in this context
key_terms.قَبَّلَهُ: kissed him, referring to kissing the deceased
key_terms.مَسَّهُ: touched him, meaning physical contact with the deceased
key_terms.يَغْتَسِلُ: he performs ghusl, the ritual bath required in this ruling

ai.seo_question: When does touching or kissing a dead body require ghusl in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning ghusl related to the dead body. It states that the one who washes the deceased must perform ghusl, and that touching or kissing the deceased after the body has become cold requires ghusl, unlike doing so while the body is still warm.
